notes: Interim. Anchors are adult male. Sprint and Yo-Yo anchors are derived from published cricket data (see sources); figures were taken from search excerpts and should be checked against the full papers. 5-10-5 and the medicine ball throw have no agreed benchmarks yet: they are recorded but not scored (benchmark_pending). VALD tests use VALD's age-and-sex bands.

sources.sprint_10m: Weldon et al. 2021, IJSPP (PMID 34937959): 19 male international cricketers, 10 m 1.84 +/- 0.08 s. Anchors: 85 = international mean; 95 = mean - 1.25 SD; 70/55/40 = mean + 1/2/3 SD.
sources.sprint_20m: Weldon et al. 2021: 20 m 3.13 +/- 0.12 s (85 = mean; 70/55/40 = mean + 1/2/3 SD). 95 = 2.96 s, mean of 15 professional fast bowlers (Relationship between physical fitness and the physical demands of 50-over cricket in fast bowlers, Univ. of Salford repository).
sources.yoyo_ir1: Anchors in level.shuttle, scored on cumulative metres: 85 = 18.3 (Weldon et al. 2021 international mean, level 18.34); 70 = 17.4 (reported PCB pass score, unofficial source); 95 = 20.1 (2400 m, close to the fast-bowler mean 2419 m, Salford study); 55 = 16.4 and 40 = 15.4 extrapolated one level apart.
sources.ruler_drop: Davis (2000) rating bands (16-19 years, general population), via brianmac.co.uk; same as football.
sources.agility_505: Benchmarks pending: no retrievable 5-10-5 norms for cricketers (Haff & Triplett 2015 and Forster et al. 2022 to be checked).
sources.medicine_ball: Benchmarks pending: seated 4 kg chest throw; no cricket or matching-protocol norms found.
sources.arm_ratio: Shoulder ER:IR below 0.66 on the bowling arm: guideline cited for fast bowlers (Shoulder injuries in provincial male fast bowlers, SA J Sports Med); evidence is isokinetic, Dynamo is isometric.
